lifecycle.creation_reason: Two independent defects each make a freshly created worktree unable to do its job, and both were found the hard way during the MT-145 and MT-147 lanes rather than by anyone reading the code. Neither belongs to an existing microtask: MT-145's allowed paths are two cfg(test) modules, MT-147's is a workflow file, and MT-146's is the memory surface. They are grouped here because they share one acceptance surface -- can a new worktree build and test at all -- and because fixing one without the other still leaves a new worktree broken.
lifecycle.relationship_to_mt_141: Defect B lives in src/backend/handshake_core/tests/**, which MT-141 owns. This contract deliberately takes only the dependency-API repair that makes that tree COMPILE, and touches nothing else in it. MT-141's own scope is porting the suite off sqlx onto the embedded store; it is currently CLAIMED and blocked by exactly this compile failure, so repairing it here unblocks MT-141 rather than competing with it. If the Operator would rather MT-141 absorb this, close MT-148 and hand it over -- but it should not sit unowned, because it blocks every integration target in the crate.

scope.summary: Repair the two defects that stop a fresh worktree from building and testing: .surql files that arrive with CRLF and break the compiled-manifest hash, and an integration-test helper calling a tempfile API that no longer exists.
scope.embedded_mode_boundary: SurrealDB and EventLedger only. No SQLite and no PostgreSQL may be added, restored, imported, or referenced as a live backend.

defects.title: Fresh Windows checkouts get CRLF .surql files and cannot bootstrap any embedded test
defects.observed: Every embedded test in a newly created worktree fails at verify_compiled_manifest before any assertion runs. The symptom presents as schema drift, which invites misdiagnosis as a schema or migration bug.
defects.cause: .gitattributes pins .md, .mjs, .json and a long list of governance paths to eol=lf but never *.surql. git check-attr text eol on src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql returns unspecified, so a fresh Windows checkout materialises those files with CRLF. The product include_str!s them in four places and hashes the bytes, so the manifest check fails.
defects.why_it_hides: Long-lived worktrees are unaffected because their files were already LF on disk. The defect is invisible until someone creates a new worktree, which is exactly when it costs the most.
defects.fix: Add *.surql text eol=lf to .gitattributes and renormalise the affected files so the committed bytes match.
defects.care_required: This renormalises every .surql in the tree. Verify afterwards that the compiled-manifest hashes still match and that an embedded test actually bootstraps -- do not assume the attribute alone is sufficient.

defects.title: The integration test tree does not compile on any host
defects.observed: error[E0599]: no associated function or constant named `from_path` found for struct `TempDir` in the current scope --> tests/atelier_surreal_support/mod.rs:124:49, followed by: error: could not compile handshake_core (test "atelier_command_corpus_tests").
defects.cause: Cargo.toml declares tempfile = "3", which resolves to 3.27.0. TempDir::from_path no longer exists in that version and into_path is deprecated in favour of keep(). tests/atelier_surreal_support/mod.rs still calls from_path at line 124 and into_path at lines 41 and 159.
defects.why_it_hides: This is a dependency API change, not a platform difference, so it breaks everywhere. It is why cargo check --all-targets has not passed on any host, and why the MT-147 cross-platform CI job had to be scoped to --lib --bins to avoid reporting another microtask's defect as its own.
defects.fix: Either pin tempfile to a version that still has from_path, or rewrite open_existing so it does not wrap an already-existing directory in a TempDir. The second is likely correct: open_existing takes ownership of a caller-supplied path for a close-and-reopen durability proof, which is not what TempDir is for. Decide by reading the call site, not by taking this note as instruction.

acceptance_criteria: AC-148-1: git check-attr text eol on a .surql file reports eol=lf, and the committed bytes of the .surql files are LF.

AC-148-2: a brand-new worktree created from the branch can bootstrap an embedded store -- proved by running one storage-touching test in a FRESH worktree, not the one the work was done in. This is the only acceptance surface that actually proves D-148-1, because the working worktree is unaffected by construction.
AC-148-3: cargo check --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features completes with no E0599 and no could-not-compile error from the tests tree.
AC-148-4: no file outside the two allowed paths is modified. In particular nothing under src/backend/handshake_core/src/** and no other file under tests/**, which MT-141 owns.
AC-148-5: the compiled-manifest hashes still match after renormalisation, and no test that passed before now fails for a schema reason.
AC-148-6: if the tempfile repair changes what open_existing does rather than only how it says it, that behaviour change is stated explicitly rather than folded in silently.
proof_targets: PT-148-1: git check-attr output before and after, plus evidence the committed bytes changed from CRLF to LF.
PT-148-2: one storage-touching test run green in a FRESH worktree created after the fix. A pass in the working worktree proves nothing here and must not be offered as evidence.
PT-148-3: cargo check --all-targets --all-features output, quoted, showing the tests tree compiling.
PT-148-4: the diff, showing only .gitattributes and the one helper file changed.
execution_constraints: CARGO_TARGET_DIR must be an owner-scoped child of Handshake Worktrees/Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target/ with a SHORT slug. Sibling artifact roots are forbidden, including Handshake/Handshake_Artifacts and Handshake Worktrees/handshake-cargo-target. Bundled DuckDB C++ headers hit the MSVC 260-character path limit and fail with C1083 if the target path is long.
HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT must be the absolute artifacts root or embedded_test_backend refuses to start.

A warm target dir exists at handshake-cargo-target/k12-kb0902 and should be reused rather than rebuilt cold. Copying a warm target dir works: cargo accepts a relocated one, which turns a 40-minute cold build into a file copy.
cargo check --all-targets builds every one of 393 integration test binaries. Expect it to be slow and memory-hungry, and serialise linking with -j 1 if it fails with LNK1102 out of memory.
Renormalisation touches many files at once. Commit the .gitattributes change and the renormalisation together so the tree is never half-converted.
scope.risk_if_missed: Every new worktree silently cannot run embedded tests, and every integration target in the crate stays uncompilable. Both defects cost real time this session before they were understood: the CRLF one blocked a lane for hours and presented as a schema bug, and the tempfile one forced the cross-platform CI job to be narrowed so it would not report someone else's defect as its own.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Repository configuration and a test helper; no operator-visible or model-navigable surface.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: No product behaviour, command, config key, IPC channel, or navigation path changes.

risks: Proving D-148-1 in the worktree where the work was done. That worktree is unaffected by construction, so a green test there is not evidence and would be a false proof.
Adding the .gitattributes line without renormalising, leaving the committed bytes still CRLF and the defect intact while the attribute suggests otherwise.
Renormalising more broadly than intended and sweeping unrelated files into the commit.
Reaching for a tempfile version pin to avoid understanding the call site, when the helper may simply be using the wrong abstraction.
Touching anything else under tests/**, which MT-141 owns and is separately claimed.
minimum_controls: AC-148-2 and PT-148-2 require a FRESH worktree for the D-148-1 proof and explicitly reject a pass in the working one.
AC-148-5 requires the manifest hashes to be re-verified after renormalisation.
AC-148-4 and PT-148-4 bound the diff to exactly two files.
AC-148-6 forces any behaviour change in open_existing to be stated rather than folded in.

hbr_obligations.INT: No product runtime behaviour changes. The tempfile repair is confined to a test helper; if it alters what open_existing does, AC-148-6 requires that to be stated.
hbr_obligations.VIS: NOT_APPLICABLE: no GUI, operator, diagnostic, or frontend surface is touched.
hbr_obligations.QUIET: Compiles and test runs stay headless and must not foreground anything or steal focus.
hbr_obligations.STOP: No capacity, token, or session-count stop reasons. If the tempfile repair turns out to need a real behaviour decision, raise it as a finding rather than guessing.
